items.title: SCUF Gaming's Early Black Friday Sale Takes Up to 25% Off Professional-Grade Xbox and PC Controllers
items.content_text: SCUF Gaming is well-regarded amongst the esports community for making some of the best professional-grade gaming controllers on the market. Premium controllers usually command a premium price point, and SCUF is no exception, with its top-end controllers priced upwards of $200. Fortunately, starting now and running through November 8, SCUF Gaming is kicking off an early Black Friday Sale with discounts up to 25% off its Xbox and PC gaming controllers. If you're in the market for an endgame controller - especially one that's aesthetically unique - then definitely check this sale out. PlayStation gamers, you are NOT out of luck. If you're in the market for a PlayStation 5 controller, SCUF Gaming isn't currently discounting its flagship Omega PS5 controller. However, you can still score a nice discount with a limited time IGN exclusive 10% off coupon code that works only on the Omega controller . The VALOR PRO Wireless Is SCUF's Best Xbox and PC Controller The VALOR PRO Wireless is SCUF's best pro controller for Xbox and PC. The Smoke edition, which features a translucent dark gray shell, is on sale right now for $139.99 after a hefty 26% off instant discount. You can also opt for bolder color schemes like "Omen" and "Ascension" for just $20 more. This officially licensed Xbox controller has pretty much every available feature to wipe out the competition. For starters, it's equipped with SCUF's Endurance TMR joysticks. TMR joysticks are a step up from Hall Effect. Although both use electromagnetic technology with no moving parts and thus are highly resistant to stick drift, TMR joysticks offer finer control, higher precision, and are more power efficient. They also cost more to manufacture, so they're only found in top-grade controllers. The VALOR PRO's front-facing layout mirrors the tried and true Xbox asymmetrical control scheme. However, there are a bunch of upgrades here too. The L/R triggers, for example, are dual action with two separate trigger stops. With a flip of a switch, you can choose between a short-throw "mouse-click fast" action or the more standard full-throw action. There are also four additional paddle switches on the rear that can be depressed without your thumbs ever leaving the thumbsticks. Rounding out the impressive feature set include tri-mode connectivity (wireless, wired, and Bluetooth) with the wireless mode supporting Corsair's low latency SlipStream technology, sweat-resistant textured grips, and a 17-hour battery with USB-C charging. PC gamers benefit from 1,000Hz polling and greater customizability through the Valor Companion App. The VALOR PRO Wired Hall Effect Conroller Is a Great Value If you do not need wireless connectivity, then the VALOR PRO Hall Effect wireless controller value will save you loads of money. It retails for $119.99 but currently on sale for $79.99. This controller is identical in design and features to the wireless version except that it uses Hall Effect sensors instead of TMR. Hall Effect tech is not quite as precise as TMR, but it's still a significant upgrade over drift-prone analog sticks that you find in most other controllers, including expensive models like the Xbox Elite Series 2 or PS5 DualSense Edge. Quite obviously, it also lack tri-mode connectivity since there's no wireless feature. Instead, the controller connects to your Xbox or PC via a detachable USB Type-C cable. Many old school gamers still swear by wired connectivity since it eliminates any input lag concerns. The Envision Pro V2 Has Five Extra Programmable G-Keys The SCUF Envision Pro V2 is the latest generation of the Envision Pro series, and it's also on sale for $129.99 for the standard colors and $159.99 for the showstoppers. This PC-specific wireless gaming controller has a rather unique trick up its sleeve, and that is the five "G-Keys" hotkeys positioned along the bottom perimeter. Much like hotkeys on a keyboard, these keys can be bound to your most utilized actions, shortcuts, and macros within the Valor Companion App. In addition to the five G-Keys, the Envision Pro V2 features four rear paddles and two additional side action buttons, giving you a total of eleven more inputs than your traditional gamepad. The controller features a front-facing symmetrical layout with two interchangeable Hall Effect thumbsticks (short, long, domed, and concave options are included), a D-pad, XYAB buttons equipped with clicky Omron mechanical switches, and dual-action triggers. The Envision Pro V2 doesn't feature the same "tri-mode" connectivity of the VALOR PRO wireless, but it still supports Corsair's low latency SlipStream wireless technology. You can also use it as a wired controller by connecting the detachable USB Type-C cable. The internal battery delivers up to 19 hours of playtime, longer than the VALOR PRO. items.title: 007 First Light Gets Free Trial For Select PlayStation Plus Subscribers
items.excerpt: Select PlayStation Plus subscribers can try 007 First Light for free via a new trial.
items.content_text: Select PlayStation Plus subscribers can try 007 First Light for free via a new trial. 007 First Light is one of the biggest games of 2026, but you'd be forgiven for having missed it. It's been a busy year filled with a wide variety of awesome things to play. With the holiday season on the horizon, the game has already started to receive some sizable discounts , so IO Interactive is warming up potential new fans. If you have PlayStation Plus Premium or Deluxe, you can try a 1-hour trial of 007 First Light. This will allow you to play the game's prologue and some of Bond's training sections, which are actually quite fun and inventive for a video game tutorial. It's a great way to come to grips not only with how the game feels to play, but also the story and IO Interactive's take on Bond. If you like it, you can buy the game for 40% off, which brings it down to about $42. 007 First Light is one of the most well-reviewed games of 2026, with IGN giving it a 9 out of 10 and praising it for being a smart yet faithful evolution of the beloved spy franchise. "Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no game has ever managed before, developer IO Interactive has found a highly successful home for the more curated action-stealth formula of 2012’s Hitman: Absolution," reads an excerpt from our review. "Patiently paced, First Light is brimming with Bond’s trinity of gadgets, guns, and girls in a way that feels fresh but reverent, and never like parody." 007 First Light has sold over 4 million copies as of August 2026 and will presumably rack up a few more copies sold throughout the holiday season, especially if it scores some end-of-year awards. IO Interactive has also released some free post-launch updates for the game to encourage players to revisit it and is planning to drop a new story DLC before the end of the year. Next year, Nintendo Switch 2 fans will also have the opportunity to play the game when it is ported over to the console in March.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Devs Talk Songs of the Past DLC Details
items.excerpt: IGN spoke to CD Projekt Red's level design lead Miles Tost and Songs of the Past writer Paula Meissner at the Lucca Comics & Games festival about creating a distinct new corner of the Continent, the surprising importance of local booze, and why even bringing characters back from the dead doesn't necessarily mean breaking canon.
items.content_text: It's been more than a decade since The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was first released, but CD Projekt Red isn't quite finished with the game just yet. Songs of the Past , the game's third expansion, is set to arrive in 2027, bringing with it an entirely new region to explore, new monsters to hunt, and more stories to tell. But how do you expand on a game as beloved as The Witcher 3 without upsetting its notoriously dedicated fans? And how do you keep things fresh while remaining faithful to a universe with decades of established lore? IGN spoke to CD Projekt Red's level design lead Miles Tost and Songs of the Past writer Paula Meissner at the Lucca Comics & Games festival about creating a distinct new corner of the Continent, the surprising importance of local booze, and why even bringing characters back from the dead doesn't necessarily mean breaking canon. IGN: Talking about Songs of the Past, from a pure level design perspective, is there a special new mechanical hook that you're looking at for players? And also, how does the environment actively change in a way that maybe veteran players of The Witcher 3 are going to be finding something new? Miles Tost: Generally speaking, the introduction of a whole new region. And if you've played the base game and the other expansions, for us, these regions are really fun. I think they have a lot of answers for that question by themselves because we try to always make each one feel unique, not just visually, but in the sense of the traversal. Skellig, for example, has a lot of boat travel as a reliance. It's also very mountainous. No Man’s Land is a much wider space. And I think with the value of Lettin, you'll basically see also that as you move around — we're not introducing a new motion mechanic as far as I'm aware — but generally it's really important to us that when you are in an area, you have this distinct feeling of being in this space. And this goes further culturally, for example. The people of Lettin have their own cultural backdrop. There are some British influences in the aristocracy there, but also we have very, very many Polish countryside influences there. You see that in the architecture, and we usually go pretty deep in thinking about the cultural identity of these spaces. So with Skellig, we have the more Viking-esque influences, but here, these people have their own alcohol. Bracket... it's a kind of fusion between honey and beer. Other than it being a cultural export, of the area and the economical backbone of the place, it even changes how we think about monsters there. It's a fun thing to mention because — Bracket is what it's called — it's a kind of fusion between honey and beer. It feels like such a small thing, but for us it's very important, because it draws a lot on what this region is. So for the production of it, you need honey and you need hops. And so you will find both of these in the area. And other than it being a cultural export, of the area and the economical backbone of the place, it even changes how we think about monsters there. So in the demo we've shown, we're basically introducing one new monster, the Swarmion, and these guys love honey. They use hornets as a means of protection, all that stuff. And so the logical reason there is because what kind of monster would live there? So the Swarmion makes sense. So you find that this seemingly small thing of these guys having their own alcohol, and it really has this huge effect on the entire area. And so this is a bit of how we're trying to make things feel unique and special. And it goes into the quest storytelling and all of that. IGN: Obviously, The Witcher has maybe one of the deepest lores in fiction, with lots of established canon. With Songs of the Past, was there a particular piece of deep lore that was particularly tricky to untangle? And as you were putting all this together, did you have to bend any of the established canon to make the story fit? Paula Meissner: We actually do have an amazing lore team in CDPR that we are cooperating with. And these guys are just amazing. They know everything, every detail from the books, from every game, from every piece of franchise content. So we do talk with them on a regular basis to make sure that we don't say anything stupid and that we stay actually truthful to the lore. But yeah, it is a tricky question because it touches on topics that weren't revealed yet. So there were definitely challenges, but I don't know how much I can say about those. Miles Tost: The general thought is that we try to always also evolve and make things fresh. So it's really important for us to not really think in this way of like, “Oh, can we do this or can we not? If we do, how? How would we bring Regis back?" If we just told people before Blood and Wine, "Yeah, we're going to do it." A lot of the hardcore fans would probably go like, "That's impossible. He fucking vaporized. How would he?" And I think we asked ourselves those same questions, and ultimately I think we settled on something that works as an expectation where he's like, "Yeah, he's back, but he's like 10% of his power, and he's still recovering. He's only been able to recover because he's had help from this other higher vampire." Geralt, by himself, is already like, "Hey, let's just bring him back from the dead." And it works as long as you can explain it and make it make sense. And I think this is really the approach that we're trying to take. So we don't really try to retcon things, but we do try to find cool ways to expand and build on the franchise and the established lore as long as we can find ways to explain it. Paula Meissner: We often actually use discussing challenges with the lore team as [original Witcher author] Andrzej Sapkowski would do it. If you look at the books and lore of The Witcher in the books, it's such a mix of everything, to be honest. And even if you hear Sapkowski in interviews and people ask him these questions, he's often like “Whatever.” So yeah, this is the ultimate argument that we use sometimes, and sometimes it works.

items.title: The 512GB SanDisk MicroSD Express Card Drops to $91 at Newegg, Triples Your Nintendo Switch 2 Storage

items.content_text: AliExpress launched its early Black Friday sale with some great deals for gamers, including one on a Nintendo Switch 2 console and another on a well-rated Switch 2 memory card. For a limited time, the official Newegg store on AliExpress is offering the SanDisk 512GB MicroSD Express Card for just $91.05 when you apply $20 off coupon code " DBDEAL20 ". It ships locally from the United States and should get delivered within a week. Newegg is a very well-known, established company and an authorized SanDisk reseller. This is a very good deal and, with the volatile prices of flash memory these days, there's no guarantee a better deal will pop up during Black Friday. Get a 512GB Nintendo Switch 2 Memory Card for $91 The Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage and it will run out faster than you think. If you have a standard MicroSD card from your previous Switch, it won't work on the Switch 2. Although the two might look similar, the MicroSD Express card is much faster than its predecessor. The SanDisk 512GB model boasts transfer speeds of up to 800MB/s and will triple your overall Switch 2 storage. That should tide you over for quite a while. Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity. Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB). The upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will top out at about 27GB. Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage. If you're a Costco member, you can get it for a bit cheaper Costco currently has the SanDisk "Gameplay" MicroSD Express card for $89.99 with free delivery. This is probably very similar - if not identical - to the one sold at Newegg. The only caveat is that you'll need to be a Costco member to take advantage of this deal. If you're already a member, then this is hands down the best deal to get. The Samsung P9 MicroSD Express card is also on sale I wrote about a similar deal earlier this week on the Samsung P9 MicroSD Express card . It's more expensive than this deal at $99, but it's sold and shipped by Amazon, which many of you will undoubtedly feel more comfortable purchasing from. The Samsung P9 is also a card that we've personally reviewed and recommend . items.title: Play-Doh Reveals Its First Romantasy Crossover for ACOTAR Fans
items.content_text: The new A Court of Thorns and Roses book was just released last week and there's already been a ton of new merchandise attached to it. There's plushies, puzzles, necklaces, and even board games now available for ACOTAR fans in 2026. And now even Play-Doh is getting in on the romantasy bandwagon with a new Blooms bouquet kit. The Play-Doh Blooms A Court of Throns and Roses kit is up for preorder now at Amazon for $49.99 and will release on January 15, 2026. The kit includes a book vase and a Truth-teller dagger. If you're wondering why Play-Doh is suddenly making kids for adults, the answer is pretty simple: Adults are buying more toys than ever. Hasbro announced the new line of adult-focused Play-Doh back in July . “The Play-Doh brand has always been about the limitless possibilities of imagination. That feeling doesn’t fade as you grow up, it evolves,” said Brian Baker, Senior Vice President at Hasbro. “ Blooms by Play-Doh serves that need, offering a more elevated, hands-on way to slow down, get lost in the process and create something beautiful you can enjoy long after you’ve made it." The idea of adult-focused flower kits isn't new. LEGO has had its very successful Botanicals line of builds for years now and they are consistently some of the most popular sets for adults . The Play-Doh version of this concept is a little less straightforward than a package of bricks, but offers a softer look that looks a bit more organic up close. The new Play-Doh set will arrive just a few days after the release of book seven, A Court of Forgotten Melody. Sarah J. Maas has hinted that a book eight is on the way as well, though no release date has been set.

items.title: Save Over $1,000 Off the Lenovo Legion RTX 5070 Ti Gaming PC With 32GB of DDR5 RAM for Black Friday
items.excerpt: This first good deal I've seen on a Lenovo Legion gaming PC since the summer.
items.content_text: With the price of GPUs and RAM at an all-time high, it's not a surprise that deals on Lenovo gaming PCs are extremely hard to come by. In fact, the last time I posted a deal on a Legion gaming PC was back in July . Fortunately, with Black Friday fast approaching, I'm back in the hunt for good gaming PC deals, and Lenovo has finally put up some newsworthy deals. For a limited time, you can get a Lenovo Legion Tower 5 RTX 5070 Ti gaming PCs for just $2,256.24 with free delivery when you apply stackable coupon codes " EXTRAFIVE " and " LENOVODEAL ". The RTX 5070 Ti is our best reviewed Nvidia GeForce Blackwell card and has the chops to run pretty much any game in 4K at 60fps or higher. Lenovo Legion RTX 5070 Ti Gaming PC for $2,256.24 The Lenovo Legion Tower 5 Gen 10 gaming PC is equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX desktop processor, GeForce RTX 5070 Ti graphics card, 32GB of DDR5-5600MHz RAM, and a 1TB M.2 SSD. The 255HX is traditionally a laptop-class CPU, and it's important to note that laptop CPUs are (permanently) soldered onto the, in this case, Intel HM870 mATX motherboard. Unlike a desktop CPU, a laptop CPU cannot be upgraded. If you do plan on swapping the CPU for something better in the future, then you'll have to stick with a gaming PC equipped with a traditional desktop CPU. If you don't intend on swapping the CPU, then you'll get excellent desktop-level performance out of this chip. The RTX 5070 Ti GPU offers solid 4K gaming performance without pricing gamers out The RTX 5070 Ti is our best reviewed Blackwell card because it offers the best bang for your buck in terms of 4K gaming performance. It performs neck-and-neck with the previous generation RTX 4080 Super and pulls ahead in any game that supports multi-frame generation, especially with the DLSS 4.5 update . It is fully capable of running any game in 4K at 60fps, including Death Stranding 2 and Crimson Desert . The RTX 5070 Ti also comes equipped with 16GB of VRAM like the RTX 5080, making it viable for AI work. Since this GPU is impossible to find as a standalone card for under $999.99, buying a prebuilt computer is the only way to avoid a markup. items.content_text: A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry. A video showing the couple facing off in Riot’s tactical first person shooter has racked up nearly three million views in just one day. In the clip, the bride — decked out in her wedding finery and delicate hair ornaments — takes virtual shots at her soon-to-be lawfully wedded opponent, who sits across from her while a group of friends and family look on in amusement. While this is certainly a unique way to celebrate one’s nuptials, it isn’t totally out of the ordinary. In fact, pre-wedding challenges like these are actually part of Chinese culture. They’re called ‘door games,’ and they’re a playful, lighthearted way to prepare for the actual ceremony and following reception. Traditionally, these are silly tasks organized by bridesmaids that the groom must successfully complete in order to ‘earn’ the right to actually marry his bride. They usually take place the morning before the wedding at the home of the bride’s family, and his groomsmen are often enlisted to help. It’s a symbolic way of making the groom ‘prove his worth’ before he takes the bride’s hand in marriage. Door games can be anything the bridesmaids choose, really; according to China Insider, these generally involve tasks like eating unusual foods, athletic challenges like doing push-ups, or testing their knowledge with trivia. In this case, the bridesmaids decided to put his elite gaming skills to the test — and it went so viral that even the official Valorant Instagram account took notice. “Wait, the wife is lowkey locked in,” it said in a comment. “The problem is if he wins, she will remember it for life, and he would not hear the end of it, but if he doesn’t, it would be near impossible to find another gem like her,” one viewer joked, while another called it the true definition of “skill-based matchmaking.” Even the CEO of pro esports team GAM commented, saying, “How do we sign her?” This is the latest gamer wedding to go viral after a Pokémon fan was able to fund his wedding by selling a trio of rare Charizard cards that had been stored in his attic for a mind-boggling $44,000. And in 2024, a streamer couple took social media by storm for their Black Ops 6-themed wedding that they held at the Call of Duty Next event in Washington, D.C. Now, that’s true love.
items.title_en: Bride Goes Viral After Challenging Groom to Beat Her at Valorant Before Marrying Her

Xbox head Asha Sharma recently said there’s more demand than Xbox consoles available , and Microsoft told told Xbox owners to trade in their dusty consoles . Meanwhile, over on the other side of the aisle, Sony wants to buy your PS5 for $400 , and anyone in the market for a PS5 Pro may have to shell out as much as $1,400 to a reseller to get one. Console stock must be getting pretty dire, right? To answer that question, I visited all the major online retailers to see what the status is surrounding console availability. And what I found was, with the exception of the PS5 Pro, every current model of every current console is widely available at manufacturer-suggested retail price (MSRP). Featured in this article Now, that doesn't mean that's how things will stay as GTA 6 and Black Friday creep nearer. And it's worth noting that those MSRPs have gone up in recent years. But at least at this pre-Black Friday, pre-GTA 6 moment in time, it’s not hard to find a new game console at retail price – unless you want a PS5 Pro. items.title: Ubisoft Among Suitors Trying to Buy Marvel's Blade, Dishonored Studio Arkane Lyon from Xbox
items.excerpt: Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox "reset."
items.content_text: Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox " reset ." According to a new report from Bloomberg, at least three companies have submitted bids to Microsoft so far, with Assassin's Creed publisher Ubisoft among them. The identities of the other bidders are not yet publicly known, but Microsoft has not accepted any bids yet. Bloomberg states that a deal would allow Arkane Lyon to complete its current project, Marvel's Blade, which the outlet says "is expected to be released within the next year or two." Arkane's other studio in Austin, Texas, was closed by Microsoft in 2024 as part of a larger series of project cuts and personnel layoffs. The Austin team had been responsible for the critically acclaimed studio's only flop, 2023's disappointing co-op vampire-hunting game Redfall, which IGN gave a 4 out of 10 in our review . Previously, Arkane Austin developed the buggy-at-launch-but-quickly-fixed immersive sim Prey as well as the beloved original Dishonored. Arkane Lyon, meanwhile, was responsible for the 10-out-of-10 first-person immersive sim Deathloop along with the outstanding Dishonored 2. Four studios have been spun out of Xbox so far rather than being immediately shut down as part of the "reset": Double Fine, which has gone independent ; Compulsion Games, which has also gone independent ; Undead Labs, which has gone independent but signed a publishing deal with an unidentified company for State of Decay 3; and Ninja Theory, which unfortunately might close down after Microsoft had two deals for another company to acquire it fall through .

items.title: Netflix Calls Its New AI Discover Feature a 'Test Kitchen' to Tailor Viewers' Recommendations
items.excerpt: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide.
items.content_text: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide. We’ve all been there; like Clueless’s Cher looking into her closet and exclaiming in dismay that there’s simply "nothing to wear," there are certainly times when it seems like streaming services have lots of shows and movies on offer, but nothing that’s appealing in the immediate moment. Netflix is attempting to help with this conundrum with its latest tool, titled AI Discover. Announced on November 3, it sits on the top bar of the TV app on the far right. Open it up, and Netflix’s AI will conjure up a few themes to choose from. The streamer’s example of this includes themes like Outsmart Everyone, Family Scandal Sagas, and Royal Court Intrigue. As told in an explainer on Netflix’s website , some of these themes match “how you want to feel,” the people you’re watching with, or how much time you have, while others are based around your recent watch history or more popular trending picks. After choosing one of these themes, Netflix’s AI will bring up similar recommendations, presenting more specific themes until the perfect show or movie arises. And if you’re simply not finding anything interesting, you can refresh your search by choosing ‘Something Different.’ Similar to Netflix’s My List option, you can also hit a ‘Tune Your Recommendations’ button, which sits next to your list and Play. This will let you save a recommendation from the AI, or tell it not to recommend a show you aren’t interested in seeing. In an official statement, Netflix described the tool as its “test kitchen,” saying that it’s “trying out new recipes for discovery, and your use and feedback help us decide which ones to keep, improve, or serve up next. Some may even make their way into the main Netflix experience.” “What we’re most excited about is how it feels to use,” the statement continues. “Tell us what you’re after, and the experience adjusts. Tell us a recommendation isn’t for you, and we’ll remember it in AI Discover, so it won’t keep turning up. AI Discover is powered by a new intelligence layer we’ve been building that responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning.” AI Discover is rolling out to US-based members who use the service in English on supported TVs, and will gradually release for more users over the coming weeks. Netflix is the latest of several major streaming services and entertainment platforms to add AI features in its product; Spotify went so far as to introduce AI DJs that will mix music for you , while Roku infamously added a 24/7 AI channel with series that are totally generated with artificial intelligence. Netflix, for its part, simply wants to better tailor viewers’ recommendations, though we’ll see what the public sentiment ends up looking like as more subscribers use it.
items.title_en: Netflix Calls Its New AI Discover Feature a 'Test Kitchen' to Tailor Viewers' Recommendations

items.title: Police Mock Car Chase Criminal for Getting Arrested Right Before GTA 6 Release
items.excerpt: Police in Derbyshire, UK, are going viral after making a TikTok video mocking a criminal who led them on a high-speed car chase, saying the suspect will now miss out on GTA 6’s highly-anticipated launch as a consequence of their actions.
items.content_text: Police in Derbyshire, UK, are going viral after making a TikTok video mocking a criminal who led them on a car chase, saying the suspect will now miss out on GTA 6’s highly-anticipated launch as a consequence of their actions. The short video, uploaded to TikTok on November 3, shows law enforcement officers from the Derbyshire county constabulary chasing a black van through residential streets as the song ‘Flower in a Hurricane’ from the GTA 6 soundtrack plays. The video leaned into the Grand Theft Auto series aesthetic; whoever edited the clip put GTA 6’s unmistakable UI over top, giving the criminal a three-star rating, and even included a minimap in the corner of the screen that followed his bungled escape. Eventually, police were able to cut him off and make an arrest. According to the post’s caption, the incident took place in the town of Ripley. The suspect, 28-year-old Jack Vickrage, has been sentenced to 14 months in prison for “admitting dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, drug-driving, and cannabis possession.” “Could've just waited a few more weeks for GTA 6 to drop... Now Jack's in prison for release day," the constabulary captioned its post. "Thirteen years is a long time to wait for the game, but nothing excuses driving like this in real life. Cutting corners and hurtling through residential streets with pedestrians and other vehicles in the middle of the day... save that stuff for the streets of Vice City.” Commenters were thoroughly impressed by the short video, urging the department to “give the admin early access [to GTA 6]” and saying the “admin needs a raise.” “15 more days to go, he can watch us play from prison,” another joked. GTA 6 launches on November 19. Just this morning, Rockstar confirmed the game’s install size and global release times , saying the preload file can measure up to 212 GB depending on your device. “Make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” the developer said. It’s shaping up to be one of the biggest pop culture events in history, with Rockstar going all-out on marketing; they partnered with Miami, Florida for a Vice City-themed takeover and collaborated with the Miami Heat to give them special, GTA 6-themed jerseys . Xbox even debuted an alligator-shaped Xbox Series X today in keeping with the game’s Florida setting, which players can win if they enter a sweepstakes. (And no, it’s not a real alligator.) There’s just two more weeks until GTA 6 is finally in players’ hands; in the meantime, oodles of fans have made plans to take off work to play it , while others are planning to call out sick on the day. Others are so amped about it that they even said they would abandon their pets for a month if they had the chance to play it early in a recent survey.
items.title_en: Police Mock Car Chase Criminal for Getting Arrested Right Before GTA 6 Release

The Xbox Series X-Bite, as it’s been affectionately dubbed by the company, is a 5-foot-long, alligator-shaped, fully functional Xbox Series X. It’s quite convincing, actually, and it even looks like a piece of genuine taxidermy. Thankfully, that’s not the case; this life-sized fake alligator was created in partnership with John Nolan Studio, which created special effects for Netflix’s The Witcher series, Jurassic World Dominion , and HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter show. To turn on the console, simply push the Xbox button on the gator’s back; it’s got a controller placed carefully in its jaws, bearing tooth marks as proof of its ravenous appetite. Even the pupils in its eyes are shaped like an X, outlined in green in keeping with Xbox branding. This strange blend of technology and artwork isn’t an avante-garde installation sitting in the Microsoft corporate offices; starting today, November 3, fans can enter a sweepstakes to win the quirky console for themselves. Here’s how to participate: Follow @XBOX on your platform of choice. (X, Instagram, or TikTok) Your profile must be public. Repost the designated XBOX sweepstakes post. Manually add #XbiteSweepstakes to your repost. The sweepstakes lasts until 11:59pm PT on November 10, 2026. The lucky winner will have 48 hours to claim the console; if they fail to do so, the gator will “make a clean getaway.” Additionally, the sweepstakes is only open to legal residents of the 50 U.S. and D.C. who are 18 years of age or older. While Xbox didn’t directly mention GTA 6 in its posts about this unique contest, it’s hard not to see why it was made; the game takes place in a fictional version of Florida, which, as most folks will know, is home to all sorts of critters, including alligators. (It’s unclear if players will be able to wrassle gators bare-handed like they do in real-life Florida, but we figure the X-Bite is the next best thing.) GTA 6 launches on November 19 on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S. (Or the X-Bite.) Just this morning, its install size and global release times were revealed, with preload dates also confirmed for November 9 and 10. Given that the file size is 212 GB, Rockstar has urged players to preload the game on their consoles as soon as they can. “Make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” Rockstar said on the game’s official website. Fans are more keen than ever to get their hands on a copy of GTA 6, to the point where oodles of IGN’s readers are actually calling out of work to play it . A separate survey from Unwind Media even shared some concerning statistics that showed a baffling amount of players are so desperate to play the game early that they would even give up their pets if that meant they could experience it a week before launch.

items.content_text: You don't have to wait until Black Friday to score a discount on one of the best controllers for PS5 and PC gamers with tourney-level skills. For a limited time, SCUF is offering its flagship Omega Wireless TMR controller starting at $198 with free shipping after you apply IGN's exclusive 10% off coupon code " IGN10 ". Professional grade controllers generally command a premium price point, and SCUF is no exception, with its top-end controllers priced upwards of $200. Save 10% Off the Ultimate PlayStation 5 Controller The officially licensed SCUF Omega PlayStation 5 controller is, frankly, what the DualSense Edge should have been. It adopts the DualSense's familiar layout with dual analog sticks and iconic geometric face buttons, but just about every component has been upgraded. For starters, both analog sticks are equipped with SCUF's Endurance TMR sensors. TMR joysticks are a step up from Hall Effect. Although both use electromagnetic technology with no moving parts and thus are highly resistant to stick drift, TMR joysticks offer finer control, higher precision, and are more power efficient. They also cost more to manufacture, so they're only found in top-grade controllers. The D-pad and face buttons are equipped with clicky Omron mechanical switches which provide satisfying tactile feedback. The L2/R2 triggers are dual action with two separate trigger stops. With a flip of a switch, you can choose between a short-throw "mouse-click fast" action or the more standard full-throw action. There are also six additional buttons - four rear paddle switches and two side buttons (exclusive to SCUF) - that can be depressed without your thumbs ever leaving the thumbsticks. As if that still wasn't enough inputs, five "G-Keys" are positioned along the bottom edge of the controller, with two of the keys being programmable via the SCUF mobile app. Note that this controller is also compatible with PC. items.title: November’s Humble Choice Is Live, and It’s Full of Bangers
items.excerpt: November’s Humble Choice is live, and it’s full of bangers, including Mafia: The Old Country, The Outer Worlds 2, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance, and more.
items.content_text: It’s the first Tuesday of November, and that can only mean one thing. Nope, not that today’s election day in the US, even though it is. It means a new Humble Choice bundle of PC games is available for super cheap ($14.99 to be exact). This month’s lineup is one for the ages. It includes Mafia: The Old Country, The Outer Worlds 2, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance, and more. Humble Choice November 2026 All told, you get eight games, all but one of which are redeemable on Steam. The code for The Outer Worlds 2 only works on Battle.net . Here’s a full list of the games included. Humble Choice Games for November 2026 Mafia: The Old Country The Outer Worlds 2 (Battle.net) Shinobi: Art of Vengeance Yakuza 6: Song of Life Crisol: Theater of Idols Space Haven Dysmantle Squeakross: Home Squeak Home Mafia: The Old Country is the latest in the series and got an 8/10 in our review . Critic Luke Reilly wrote, “Mafia: The Old Country is a conventional but effective return to the linear and tightly story-driven format of the original Mafia and Mafia II, and it boasts a wonderful eye and ear for detail.” The Outer Worlds 2 also got an 8/10 , with reviewer Travis Northup writing, “The Outer Worlds 2 doesn’t try to rewrite Obsidian’s RPG playbook, but it’s yet another strong refinement, with smoother combat, diabolically compelling buildcrafting and loot, and a story that immediately made me want to start again to see an alternate outcome.” I’m also personally looking forward to playing Squeakross, because I love Picross puzzles, and it’s full of them. It looks colorful and super fun; it's been on my Steam wishlist ever since it came out. Overall, you can’t really go wrong with this month’s selections. If you just want this month’s games, you can get it for $14.99 and then cancel your subscription. The games are yours to keep forever. Alternatively, you can save some money buy buying an annual subscription for $154.99, which saves you a little over $24 versus paying month to month. Humble Choice members also get a handful of other benefits from the subscription. You get up to 20% off games in the Humble Store. You get access to a vault of games that’s always available as long as you’re currently a member. And a portion of your membership goes to charity. This month’s charity is Covenant House , which helps provide 24/7 safe shelter, food, medical and mental healthcare, and supportive services to young people experiencing homelessness. For more deals, check out our full Black Friday coverage, which believe it or not, has already begun.
